hook_text: That yellow hill on the edge of town is not a hill at all.
clip_script: Germiston, Gauteng. A flat-topped yellow hill: a mine dump, crushed rock left after gold was taken out. On the desks: coal, iron ore, gold-flecked rock, a rough diamond. These are minerals, natural, solid substances from the Earth's crust. They took millions of years to form, so once we use them, they are gone. They are non-renewable. The sun and wind won't run out. South Africa is rich in minerals, but they won't last forever.
visual_style: Whiteboard mine dump on a skyline, rock samples sorted into two piles, then a sun and wind turbine on the renewable side.
mood: Thoughtful and curious, like discovering a hidden treasure.
pacing: Starts with a mystery hill, then sorts the samples step by step.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find three things at home made from minerals.
